exposure: Gestational diabetes mellitus diagnosed before 22 weeks (GDM(<22))
Gestational diabetes mellitus diagnosed between 22 and 30 weeks (GDM(22-30))
Gestational diabetes mellitus diagnosed after 30 weeks (GDM(>30))
cohort: 695,912 women in France who gave birth in 2018, including 84,705 women with hyperglycaemia in pregnancy
finding: Compared with GDM diagnosed at 22-30 weeks, overt diabetes, GDM diagnosed before 22 weeks, and to a lesser extent GDM diagnosed after 30 weeks were associated with poorer maternal-fetal outcomes.
mod_finding: Caesarean sections were more frequent in women with overt diabetes (adjusted prevalence ratio 1.54, 95% CI 1.39-1.72) and women without hyperglycaemia in pregnancy were less likely to have a caesarean section (adjusted prevalence ratio 0.80, 95% CI 0.79-0.82).
